# Fenrir Antivirus: full guide

Endpoint protection: antivirus and EDR with a security operations console. This guide takes you from an empty server to daily use of Fenrir Antivirus on its own.

**Contents:** [What you get](#what-you-get) · [Before you start](#before-you-start) · [Install](#install) ·
[First sign-in](#first-sign-in) · [First steps](#first-steps) · [The pages](#the-pages) ·
[Configuration](#configuration) · [Agents](#agents) · [Everyday use](#everyday-use) ·
[Users, roles and security](#users-roles-and-security) · [Updates](#updates) · [Backups](#backups) ·
[Adding more apps later](#adding-more-apps-later) · [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting) · [More reading](#more-reading)

## What you get

Fenrir Antivirus is for teams who want to protect, watch and respond on Windows, Linux and macOS endpoints. It is one of the [Fenrir apps](../README.md): the
same code as the complete platform, run with `FENRIR_APP=av`, so the server serves only this app's pages and
background jobs, and the dashboard shows only this app. Customers, users, roles, settings, webhooks, API credentials
and the audit log are part of every app.

- Real-time and scheduled scanning with signatures, YARA and a static malware model; AMSI integration on Windows
- EDR telemetry with Sigma-compatible detection rules and correlation into incidents
- Response: isolate a device, kill a process, quarantine and restore files, collect a forensic bundle
- Managed Microsoft Defender on Windows (settings, exclusions, health)
- Encrypted DNS filtering that follows devices on and off the network
- Threat intelligence from your signature feed plus your own indicators and YARA rules
- Threat hunting over raw telemetry, response rules and SOC maintenance windows
- Web protection for iPhone, iPad and Mac through a DNS profile (no agent needed)

Not in this app: Patching, scripts and remote desktop (the **rmm** app), vulnerability management (**vuln**), tickets (**psa**). Without the PSA, "open a ticket" steps in response rules and incidents are skipped; the alert and incident remain the record.

## Before you start

| Item | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Server | Linux (Ubuntu 24.04 LTS on amd64 recommended), 4 vCPUs, 8 GB RAM plus 4 GB swap, 80 GB SSD. 16 GB RAM makes the first build faster. |
| Software | Docker Engine with buildx and Docker Compose 2.24.4 or newer, Git, curl, OpenSSL, Bash, Python 3. |
| Network | A domain name (DNS A record) pointing at the server; TCP 80 and 443 open; SSH restricted to you. Devices must reach the server over HTTPS. |
| Signing (optional) | A Windows code-signing certificate (.pfx). Without one, Windows agents are built unsigned and SmartScreen warns. |

You also need an email address for the first administrator and for the HTTPS certificate (Let's Encrypt, issued
automatically).

## Install

### 1. Your own copy

Run the app from **your own copy** of this repository, so you decide when changes reach your server:

- **Public fork**: on GitHub select **Fork**.
- **Private copy**: create an empty private repository, then:

  ```bash
  git clone --bare https://github.com/ORIGINAL-OWNER/ORIGINAL-REPO.git fenrir-tmp.git
  cd fenrir-tmp.git && git push --mirror https://github.com/YOUR-ACCOUNT/YOUR-PRIVATE-REPO.git
  cd .. && rm -rf fenrir-tmp.git
  ```

Never commit `deploy/.env`, `deploy/signing/` or backups; `.gitignore` already excludes them.

### 2. Prepare the server

```bash
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y git curl openssl ca-certificates python3
```

Install Docker Engine, buildx and Compose from [Docker's instructions](https://docs.docker.com/engine/install/ubuntu/),
then check them:

```bash
sudo docker compose version
sudo docker run --rm hello-world
```

Add swap if the server has less than 8 GB of RAM (the first build needs it):

```bash
sudo fallocate -l 4G /swapfile && sudo chmod 600 /swapfile && sudo mkswap /swapfile && sudo swapon /swapfile
echo '/swapfile none swap sw 0 0' | sudo tee -a /etc/fstab
```

Create a DNS **A record** for your domain (for example `av.yourcompany.com`) pointing at the server, remove any
wrong AAAA record, and allow TCP 80 and 443 in the provider's and the server's firewall.

### 3. Run setup

```bash
git clone https://github.com/YOUR-ACCOUNT/YOUR-COPY.git ~/fenrir
cd ~/fenrir
deploy/setup.sh --app av
```

Setup asks for your domain, the administrator email and your organisation's name, whether you have a Windows code-signing certificate and an optional signature feed. It writes `deploy/.env` with fresh random
secrets and `FENRIR_APP=av`, sets up the HTTPS proxy, creates the release-signing key, prints the administrator
password **once**, and offers to build and start the server. It never overwrites an existing `deploy/.env`.

Scripted install:

```bash
deploy/setup.sh --app av --domain av.yourcompany.com --email you@yourcompany.com --name "Your Company" --yes
```

### 4. Build and start

If you did not let setup start it, use the command it printed (also saved in `deploy/.compose-files`). A helper
saves typing; define it in each new shell, from `~/fenrir`:

```bash
dc() { sudo env COMPOSE_BAKE=false docker compose $(cat deploy/.compose-files) --env-file deploy/.env "$@"; }
dc up -d --build
dc ps
```

The first build takes a while. Then check:

```bash
curl --fail https://av.yourcompany.com/health
curl --fail https://av.yourcompany.com/api/app      # shows "key": "av"
```

### 5. Schedule backups and run the go-live check

```bash
echo "17 2 * * * root cd $PWD && FENRIR_COMPOSE_FILES=$PWD/deploy/docker-compose.https.yml deploy/backup.sh /var/backups/fenrir >> /var/log/fenrir-backup.log 2>&1" \
  | sudo tee /etc/cron.d/fenrir-backup
sudo deploy/preflight.sh
```

Fix anything the go-live check reports as FAIL before relying on the server. The full checklist is in
[go-live](../../docs/GO_LIVE.md).

## First sign-in

1. Open `https://av.yourcompany.com` and sign in with the administrator email and the password setup printed.
2. Set up two-step sign-in when asked (an authenticator app or a passkey). Staff accounts must have it.
3. Change the password in Settings → Account.
4. Check Settings → Platform for readiness findings.

The menu shows only this app's pages; the title in the corner is **Fenrir Antivirus**.

## First steps

1. **Add a customer.** Settings → Tenants → New tenant. Pick a policy template (balanced is a good start).
2. **Install an agent.** Deploy agents → choose the operating system and customer → download and run the installer. The device appears in Devices within a minute.
3. **Test detection safely.** Open the device → run the built-in "Validate real-time protection (EICAR test)" script. An alert appears in Alerts and the test file in Quarantine.
4. **Tune the policy.** Protection policies → open the default policy: real-time protection, scan schedule, ransomware protection, DNS filtering categories, Defender settings.
5. **Connect a signature feed** (optional, recommended) so agents receive new indicators and rules. See [your own threat feed](../../components/signaturedb/README.md).
6. **Set exclusions** for line-of-business software in EDR exclusions before rolling out widely.

## The pages

| Menu | Page | What it is for |
|---|---|---|
| Triage | **Dashboard** | Protected devices, open incidents, threats stopped, alerts per day, the riskiest devices, top detections and the MITRE ATT&CK techniques seen. |
| Triage | **Inbox** | Everything that needs someone in one list. Repeats collapse into one item: the same detection on 40 devices is one line. Take an item, snooze it, or act on it in one click. |
| Triage | **Alerts** | Every rule hit at medium or above. Related alerts on a device roll up into one incident. Take an alert to own it, or snooze it. |
| Triage | **Incidents** | Correlated attacks with a guided response playbook and automated actions (isolate, kill, quarantine). |
| Triage | **Threat hunting** | Search raw telemetry across every device, or replay any Sigma rule over history before deploying it. |
| Triage | **Threat intel** | Indicators and YARA rules from your signature feed plus your own, pushed to agents and DNS in minutes. |
| Endpoints | **Devices** | Every enrolled device. Open one for its health, system details, software, activity, remote session and effective policy. |
| Endpoints | **Device groups** | Organise each customer's devices, give groups their own policy, and target them with actions. |
| Endpoints | **Protection policies** | What agents do: scanning, real-time protection, DNS filtering, monitoring, updates, phone rules. One default per customer, overridable per group. |
| Endpoints | **Protection health** | Whether every endpoint is protected, on the current agent, scanning and reporting in. Degraded protection raises an alert. |
| Endpoints | **Agent health** | Whether each agent is on the current build (and why not), and what it reported failing in the last 7 days. |
| Endpoints | **Quarantine** | Files agents have isolated. Restore a false positive or delete a confirmed threat. |
| Endpoints | **Deploy agents** | Choose an operating system and customer, then download an installer that enrols itself. |
| Identity, cloud & network | **DNS protection** | Encrypted DNS filtering that follows every device on and off the network. Categories and lists are set in each policy. |
| Admin | **Detection rules** | Sigma-compatible rules with correlation. Import community rules or write your own. |
| Admin | **Response rules** | When an alert matches, queue response actions or call webhooks. |
| Admin | **EDR exclusions** | Paths, hashes and processes the agents should not act on, per customer or globally. |
| Admin | **SOC maintenance** | Temporarily suppress a detection rule for one customer; events stay available for hunting. |
| Admin | **Settings** | Customers (tenants), users and roles, custom fields, region and holidays, webhooks, API credentials, approvals, the audit log and platform options. |

## Configuration

Settings live in `deploy/.env` (restart with `dc up -d` after a change) and in the console's Settings page.

### Signature feed

Setup asks for a feed URL. Without one, agents use the rules and model shipped with the server. To run your own feed see [components/signaturedb](../../components/signaturedb/README.md).

### Blocking before a program runs

On Windows, pre-execution blocking comes from Microsoft Defender, which Fenrir manages; Fenrir ships no kernel driver. See [ransomware protection](../../docs/RANSOMWARE_PROTECTION.md).

### Exclusions and the DNS proxy

See [EDR exclusions and the DNS proxy](../../docs/EDR_EXCLUSIONS_AND_DNS_PROXY.md).

### Apple devices

iPhone, iPad and Mac get web protection from a configuration profile, without an agent. See [Apple web protection](../../docs/APPLE_WEB_PROTECTION.md).

### Your branding and email

- `FENRIR_MSP_NAME`: your organisation's name (or change it in Settings).
- `FENRIR_SMTP_HOST`, `FENRIR_SMTP_PORT`, `FENRIR_SMTP_USER`, `FENRIR_SMTP_PASSWORD`, `FENRIR_SMTP_FROM`: outgoing
  email for alerts, reports and sign-in messages. Leave empty to send none.

## Agents

- **Install**: Deploy agents → choose the operating system and customer → download. The installer carries a
  one-time enrolment token for that customer, so the device lands in the right place. On Windows run it as
  administrator; on Linux and macOS with `sudo`. See [agent downloads](../../docs/AGENT_DEPLOYMENT_DOWNLOADS.md).
- **Approve**: with `FENRIR_OPEN_ENROLLMENT=false` (the default from setup) only installers from Deploy agents can
  enrol. Devices that enrol without a token wait in the *Unassigned* customer for approval.
- **Update**: agents update themselves after a server rebuild that changes agent code, pilot devices first. Watch
  progress in Settings → Agent releases and Agent health.
- **Remove**: open the device → **Decommission device**. That ends its remote sessions, cancels its queued commands
  and revokes its key, so the agent stops reporting. It stays installed: uninstall it on the machine (Windows, as
  administrator: `fenrir-agent-service.exe --uninstall`).
- **Signing**: Windows agents are signed only if you gave setup a code-signing certificate
  ([code signing](../../docs/CODE_SIGNING.md)). Linux and macOS updates are signed with the release key setup created
  in `deploy/signing/` (back it up).

## Everyday use

- Work the Inbox: take an item, decide, resolve or snooze. Critical and high items with no owner are the priority.
- Open incidents follow a guided playbook; isolate first if in doubt, then investigate with Threat hunting.
- Check Protection health for devices with protection off, old builds or no recent scan.
- Release false positives from Quarantine and add a precise exclusion so they do not return.

## Users, roles and security

- **Users**: Settings → Users → invite. Each user gets a role and the customers they can see.
- **Roles**: built-in roles (platform admin, MSP admin, technician, analyst, billing, viewer, customer roles) and your
  own on the Roles tab.
- **Two-step sign-in** is required for staff (`FENRIR_REQUIRE_MFA=true`). Passkeys are supported.
- **Approvals**: Settings → Approvals can require a second person for sensitive or bulk actions.
- **Audit log**: every change is recorded in a tamper-evident log (Settings → Audit log → Verify integrity).
- **API credentials and webhooks**: Settings → API credentials for scripts; Settings → Webhooks to send events to
  other systems.

## Updates

Your server follows **your** copy of the repository. To take new releases, use **Sync fork** on GitHub (or pull from
the original repository into your copy), then on the server:

```bash
cd ~/fenrir && git pull && dc up -d --build
```

Or turn on automatic updates so the server follows your copy's `main` branch: see [auto update](../../docs/AUTO_UPDATE.md).
Your data, `deploy/.env` and keys are kept across updates.

## Backups

The nightly job from step 5 saves the database, uploaded files (evidence, bundles) and signed release manifests to
`/var/backups/fenrir`. It does **not** include `deploy/.env` or `deploy/signing/`, on purpose: keep those in an offline
password manager or safe, because without the same `FENRIR_VAULT_KEY` a restored database's stored secrets cannot be
read. Copy backups off the server too. Restore steps: [backup and restore](../../docs/BACKUP_AND_RESTORE.md).

## Adding more apps later

All apps share one database design, so switching keeps your data:

1. Edit `deploy/.env` and set `FENRIR_APP=complete` (everything) or another app.
2. Restart: `dc up -d`.
3. Reload the console: the menu now shows the new app's pages, and the data you already have is there.

Switching back hides the other app's pages again; nothing is deleted. Work one app would hand to another (for
example a ticket from an alert) happens only while both run on the same server.

## Troubleshooting

### The site does not load

Check the DNS record points at the server, ports 80 and 443 are open, and the containers are running (`dc ps`,
`dc logs --tail=100 cloud caddy`). The certificate is issued a minute after DNS reaches the server.

### The menu shows the wrong app

`curl https://YOUR-DOMAIN/api/app` shows which app the server runs. Check `FENRIR_APP` in `deploy/.env`, then
`dc up -d` and reload the page.

### Signed out straight away or "session expired"

`FENRIR_SECRET_KEY` changed. Keep it stable; it signs sessions.

### A trusted program is quarantined

Restore it from Quarantine, then add an exclusion by hash or signed publisher (not a broad folder) in EDR exclusions.

### No alerts at all

Run the EICAR test script on one device. If nothing appears, check Protection health for that device and that its policy has real-time protection on.
